rag.description: Send a UDP datagram from an automation to command a device, post a metric or a log line, or query a service. The step can wait for the reply, retry on silence, and collect broadcast answers, so a flow gets proof of delivery and a value it can assert or branch on.

qa.answer: It sends one UDP datagram to a host and port, and on request waits for the reply and stores it.
qa.question: What does the SendUdpMessage plugin do?

qa.answer: Host, Port, and Message or MessageFile are required; Format selects Text, Hex, or Base64; WaitForResponse, Timeout, Retries, MaxResponses, and AnySender control replies. The outputs are BytesSent, Response, ResponseCount, Responses, RemoteAddress, and RemotePort.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of SendUdpMessage?

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the upload icon and the ActionRuleModel, alone or beside StartUdpListener and ReceiveUdpMessage.
qa.question: How does SendUdpMessage fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Set WaitForResponse when the flow needs a reply, add Retries on a lossy network, add AnySender for a device that answers from another address, and send through a Listener without WaitForResponse when replies arrive late or more than once.
qa.question: What are best practices for using SendUdpMessage?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “SendUdpMessage” and pass inputs in the argument, such as {{$ --Host:192.168.1.50 --Port:5005 --Message:PING --WaitForResponse}}.
qa.question: How is a SendUdpMessage rule configured?

qa.answer: A missing payload, a bad port, an unknown format or encoding, an unknown listener, a local port in use, or an unresolved host fails the step before sending; with WaitForResponse, silence after every attempt fails it with a timeout.

description: ### Purpose
SendUdpMessage sends one UDP datagram, a single network message, to a host and port.
It can wait for the reply, send again when none arrives, and collect several replies to a broadcast.
Flows use it to command devices, post metrics or log lines, and query services that answer over UDP.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Text and binary payloads | Sends plain text, hexadecimal bytes, Base64 bytes, or the unchanged bytes of a file. |
| Request and reply | Waits for a reply from the destination address, or from any sender with AnySender, and fails the step when none arrives within the timeout. |
| Retries | Sends the datagram again while no reply arrives, up to a set number of times. |
| Broadcast discovery | Sends to a broadcast address and collects replies until MaxResponses arrive or the timeout ends. |
| Fixed source endpoint | Binds a local port or address for devices that reply to a fixed port. |
| Shared listener socket | Sends through a started listener, so replies the step does not wait for stay buffered for later steps. |
| Reply refinement | Reads one field of a JSON reply, or one element or attribute of an XML reply, and keeps a regular-expression match. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Device control | Send a command packet to a printer, a scale, an industrial controller (PLC), or a lab instrument. |
| Metrics and logs | Post a metric counter (StatsD) or a log line (syslog) from a running process. |
| Device discovery | Broadcast a discovery request and list the devices that answer. |
| Service triggers | Notify a UDP service that a batch or a file is ready. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Protocol checks | Send a request and assert the reply of a UDP service. |
| Negative checks | Treat the timeout failure as the pass condition to prove a closed or filtered port sent no reply. |
| Test stimulus | Inject datagrams into the application under test while another step watches the UI. |
| Mock servers | Reply through the same listener to the sender a ReceiveUdpMessage step captured. |
Stores the number of payload bytes the datagram carried.
Returned in the response entity for direct data transfer.
entity.name: BytesSent

description: Stores the IP address of the sender of the first reply.
When the step does not wait for a reply it holds the resolved destination address, which shows how the host name resolved.
entity.name: RemoteAddress

description: Stores the port of the sender of the first reply.
When the step does not wait for a reply it holds the destination port.
entity.name: RemotePort

description: Stores the text of the first reply, after OnElement, OnAttribute, and RegularExpression refined it.
The ResponseFormat argument selects plain, hexadecimal, or Base64 text.
entity.name: Response

description: Stores the number of replies the step collected.
Compare it with the expected number to tell a partial result from a full one.
entity.name: ResponseCount

description: Stores every collected reply as a JSON array, oldest first.
Each item holds `Data`, `Length`, `ReceivedAt`, `RemoteAddress`, and `RemotePort`.
entity.name: Responses

edge_cases: Nothing listens on the destination port
annotations.expected_result: The step sends the UTF-8 bytes of `PING` to 192.168.1.50 on port 5005.
annotations.notes: UDP confirms no delivery, so the step passes even when nothing listens on the port. Add WaitForResponse when the flow needs proof.

description: ### Send a text datagram
The argument names the destination and the text to send.
The step sends one datagram and returns without waiting for a reply.

annotations.expected_result: The step sends the four bytes AA 55 01 00 as one datagram.
annotations.notes: Commas, colons, hyphens, and `0x` prefixes are accepted between bytes. An odd number of digits fails the step before anything is sent.

description: ### Send a binary packet written as hexadecimal
The Format parameter reads the message as hexadecimal bytes.
The spaces between the bytes are ignored, so the packet reads the way a protocol document prints it.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the reply text in `SendUdpMessage:Response` and the sender in `SendUdpMessage:RemoteAddress` and `SendUdpMessage:RemotePort`.
annotations.notes: The step fails with a timeout when all three attempts end without a reply. Each attempt waits the full timeout, so the longest wait here is six seconds. A datagram from another address does not count as the reply.

description: ### Send a request and wait for the reply
The WaitForResponse switch keeps the step waiting for a reply.
The step sends the request again up to two times when no reply arrives within two seconds.

edge_cases: Subnet broadcast address without the Broadcast switch
annotations.expected_result: The step stores every reply in `SendUdpMessage:Responses` and the number of replies in `SendUdpMessage:ResponseCount`.
annotations.notes: One reply is enough for the step to pass. Each item of the list carries the address and port of the device that answered.

description: ### Discover devices with a broadcast
The Broadcast switch allows the subnet broadcast address 192.168.1.255, which the system rejects without it.
The step collects up to ten replies and returns after three seconds or after the tenth reply.

edge_cases: Listener was stopped by an earlier step
annotations.expected_result: The step sends `START` from the port the `Telemetry` listener is bound to.
annotations.notes: Use it when a device replies later or more than once. LocalPort and LocalAddress are ignored, because the listener is already bound.

description: ### Send through a started listener
The Listener parameter sends the datagram from the socket of the listener named `Telemetry`.
Replies arrive on the listener port and stay buffered for a later ReceiveUdpMessage step.

annotations.expected_result: The step sends the decoded bytes from 192.168.1.10 port 5006 and stores the reply as hexadecimal text.
annotations.notes: A fixed source port serves devices that reply to one known port, and a local address selects the network interface. The step fails when another socket already holds the port.

description: ### Send Base64 bytes from a fixed source port
The message holds Base64 bytes and leaves from port 5006 of the interface 192.168.1.10.
The reply is published as hexadecimal text.

edge_cases: Character is not part of the encoding
annotations.expected_result: The step sends the text as Latin1 bytes and leaves the response entity empty.
annotations.notes: Use the encoding the device expects, because UTF-8 writes an accented letter as two bytes. The session parameters stay available to later steps.

description: ### Send text in a legacy encoding and keep it out of the entity
The Encoding parameter writes the accented text as Latin1 bytes.
The NoEntity switch publishes the outputs as session parameters only.

annotations.expected_result: The step sends the content of `wake.bin` to 10.0.0.20 on port 9000.
annotations.notes: Format does not apply to a file, and Encoding never changes the file bytes. Use it for a packet kept beside the flow.

description: ### Send the bytes of a file
The MessageFile parameter names a file.
The step sends its bytes unchanged as one datagram.

edge_cases: Field is missing from the reply
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the digits of the `temperature` field in `SendUdpMessage:Response`.
annotations.notes: Only the first reply is refined; `Responses` keeps the full JSON text. A path or a pattern that finds nothing stores an empty value.

description: ### Read one field of a JSON reply
The step waits for a JSON reply and reads the `temperature` field through the JSONPath in `onElement`.
A regular expression `\d+` is applied to the value attribute of the selected field and keeps its first run of digits, so 21.5 becomes 21.

edge_cases: Unrelated datagram reaches the socket first
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the first reply from any sender in `SendUdpMessage:Response` and its real sender in `SendUdpMessage:RemoteAddress`.
annotations.notes: Without AnySender a reply from another address is ignored and the step times out. With it, the first datagram that reaches the socket after the send counts, so check SendUdpMessage:RemoteAddress when unrelated traffic is possible.

description: ### Accept a reply from another address
The AnySender switch counts a reply from any address, not only from 192.168.1.50.
The step waits up to two seconds for the reply of a device that answers from a second network card.

edge_cases: Attribute is missing from the element
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the value of the `code` attribute in `SendUdpMessage:Response`.
annotations.notes: Without onAttribute the step stores the markup of the whole element. A missing element or attribute stores an empty value.

description: ### Read one attribute of an XML reply
The step waits for an XML reply and selects the `status` element through the XPath in `onElement`.
The `onAttribute` property keeps the value of its `code` attribute.
Stores the number of payload bytes the datagram carried.
Compare it with the expected packet length to confirm the payload was read as intended.
The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before comparing or displaying it.

description: Counts a datagram from any sender as a reply, not only one from the destination address.
Use it for a device that answers from another address, such as a host with several network cards.
Applies only when WaitForResponse is set.
parameters.name: AnySender

description: Allows the destination to be a broadcast address, such as `192.168.1.255`.
The operating system rejects a subnet broadcast address without it.
The limited broadcast address `255.255.255.255` is accepted with or without the switch.
parameters.name: Broadcast

description: Names the text encoding, such as `UTF8`, `ASCII`, `Unicode`, `UTF32`, `Latin1`, or a code page such as `windows-1252`.
Applies to a Text message and to replies published as text.
Defaults to UTF-8, and a name the runtime does not know fails the step.
parameters.name: Encoding

description: Selects how the Message value becomes bytes.
Defaults to Text, applies only to Message, and any other value than Text, Hex, or Base64 fails the step.
parameters.name: Format

description: Reads the value as plain text in the encoding of the step.
Use it for line protocols such as syslog, StatsD, or a device command.
values.name: Text

description: Reads the value as hexadecimal bytes, such as `AA 55 01 00`.
Spaces, commas, colons, hyphens, and `0x` prefixes between bytes are ignored.
values.name: Hex

description: Reads the value as Base64 bytes.
Use it for a binary payload, or for text that contains ` --` or `}}`, which end an inline argument value.
values.name: Base64

description: Names the destination as a host name or an IP address, such as `192.168.1.50`.
A host name is resolved before sending, and a name that does not resolve, or has no address of the socket family, fails the step.
parameters.name: Host

description: Names a listener started by StartUdpListener and sends through its socket.

Without WaitForResponse, replies stay in the listener buffer for ReceiveUdpMessage; with it, the replies the step collects are taken from the buffer, and datagrams from other senders stay unless AnySender is set or the destination is a broadcast or multicast address.
A name that is not started fails the step.
parameters.name: Listener

description: Binds the source IP address, which selects the network interface on a machine with several.
Defaults to every IPv4 interface, and an IPv6 address makes the socket an IPv6 socket.
Ignored when Listener is set.
parameters.name: LocalAddress

description: Binds the source port of the datagram, from 0 to 65535.
Defaults to 0, which lets the system pick a free port; set it for a device that replies to a fixed port.
Ignored when Listener is set.
parameters.name: LocalPort

description: Sets the number of replies that ends the wait before the timeout.
Defaults to 1; a higher value collects the answers of several devices to one broadcast.
One reply is enough for the step to pass.
parameters.name: MaxResponses

description: Holds the payload of the datagram, read according to Format.
Wins over MessageFile when both are set, and one of the two is required.
A value that contains ` --` or `}}` travels as Hex or Base64, because those sequences end an inline argument value.
parameters.name: Message

description: Names a file whose bytes are sent unchanged as the payload.
Use it for a binary packet kept beside the flow, and a missing file fails the step.
parameters.name: MessageFile

description: Leaves the response entity empty and publishes the outputs as session parameters only.
Use it when the datagram content must stay out of the extracted data of the flow.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Sets the destination port, from 1 to 65535.
Any other value fails the step before a datagram is sent.
parameters.name: Port

description: Selects how the bytes of each reply are published.
Defaults to Text, and any other value than Text, Hex, or Base64 fails the step.
parameters.name: ResponseFormat

description: Publishes each datagram as plain text in the encoding of the step.
Use it for text protocols and for JSON or XML payloads.
values.name: Text

description: Publishes each datagram as upper-case hexadecimal text without separators.
Use it to compare a binary packet byte by byte.
values.name: Hex

description: Publishes each datagram as Base64 text.
Use it to pass a binary packet to a later step without loss.
values.name: Base64

description: Sets how many times the datagram is sent again while no reply arrives.
Defaults to 0, and applies only when WaitForResponse is set.
Each attempt waits the full Timeout.
parameters.name: Retries

description: Sets how long to wait for replies after each send when WaitForResponse is set.
Accepts a number of milliseconds, such as `2000`, or a time span, such as `00:00:02`.
Defaults to 5000 milliseconds, which also replaces a value that is neither a number nor a time span.
parameters.name: Timeout

description: Waits for a reply after sending and fails the step when none arrives within Timeout.
Without it the step sends the datagram and returns at once.

Only datagrams from the destination address count as replies, unless the destination is a broadcast address, meaning any IPv4 address that ends in .255, or a multicast address, or AnySender is set, where every sender counts.
parameters.name: WaitForResponse

description: Holds the arguments of the step, such as `{{$ --Host:192.168.1.50 --Port:5005 --Message:PING}}`.
Host and Port are required, together with Message or MessageFile.
properties.name: Argument

description: Names the locator type of the rule and stays at its default for this action.
The path in OnElement is read as JSONPath for JSON text and as XPath for XML text, whatever the value is.
properties.name: Locator

description: Names one attribute of the XML element that OnElement selects.
The attribute value replaces the element as the published text, and a missing attribute publishes an empty value.
Ignored for JSON text and when OnElement is empty.
properties.name: OnAttribute

description: Selects one part of the first reply: a JSONPath such as `$.status` for JSON text, or an XPath such as `//status` for XML text.
The first result is kept: an XML element is published as its markup, and an attribute or a text node, such as `//status/@code`, as its value.
Text that is neither JSON nor XML skips the path, a path that finds nothing publishes an empty value, and a malformed path fails the step.
properties.name: OnElement

description: Keeps the first match of the pattern in the first reply, after OnElement was applied.
Defaults to a pattern that keeps the whole text, and a pattern that does not match publishes an empty value.
properties.name: RegularExpression

summary: Sends one UDP datagram, a single network message, to a host and port as text, hexadecimal bytes, Base64 bytes, or the bytes of a file.
Waits for one or more replies on request, sends again when no reply arrives, and fails the step on silence.
Stores the reply, its sender, and the reply count, so a later step can assert or branch on a device answer.
